transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-24
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Ravi Kapoor (Beacon Bank - Head of ML), Emily Santos (Platform Eng), Jordan Lee (CTO), Priya Desai (Security)

Summary: final rollout plan, canary/A-B approach, monitoring and runbook review, security gating for go-live.

[00:00] Lena Park: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about an hour, agenda is cutover plan, canary and A slash B, monitoring/runbooks, and open items. quick check, everyone able to see the doc?
[00:18] Ravi Kapoor: yes seeing it, thanks Lena.
[00:22] Marcus Chen: all good here.
[00:30] Emily Santos: yep good.

[01:05] Lena Park: cool so quick status, POC week six, load and quality metrics look stable - we've seen 98% match on intent reranking, latency at 95th is around 260ms for our tested prompts on the hosted variant. Dedicated nodes with quantization pushed 95th to 180ms. Marcus you want to add?
[01:25] Marcus Chen: yeah there was some noise on longer sequences where KV cache priming caused spikes, we pushed a small config to reduce cold cache penalties. also note that continuous batching is saving about 12% token cost on peak.
[01:45] Ravi Kapoor: good to hear. our big concerns are the cutover risk and how to quickly roll back if we see regressions in quality or a cost spike.
[02:05] Lena Park: understood. proposed cutover approach: 1) smoke test in staging, 2) low-risk canary with 5% of production traffic for 2 hours, monitor p95/p99, error rate, and token unit cost; 3) progressive ramp to 25% then 50% with automated rollback triggers. canary should use the Dedicated variant for predictable latency.
[02:35] Jordan Lee: can you clarify automatic rollback triggers? what metrics and thresholds?
[02:45] Marcus Chen: recommended triggers: p99 latency increase > 30% over baseline for 10 minutes, error rate > 1% sustained for 5 minutes, or a quality regression detected by our probe prompts (score drop > 5%). we can tie to the routing policy to divert traffic back to previous model variant.
[03:10] Emily Santos: when you say quality probe prompts, are those the eval sets we shared? how automated is that?
[03:22] Marcus Chen: yes those probe prompts are the set you provided plus some synthetic edge cases. we have a lightweight eval runner that checks n samples every minute. it's not perfect but it's enough to flag regressions for immediate rollback.

[04:05] Priya Desai: security question - during canary and cutover where logs are captured, what retention and who has access? we need SOC2-compliant audit logs and KMS integration.
[04:18] Lena Park: yes for Private/Dedicated we support KMS HSM integration and audit logs with retention configurable; default is 90 days, we can extend. we'll send the security docs.
[04:32] Priya Desai: and SAML SSO for the console?
[04:36] Lena Park: yep SAML/Okta is supported, RBAC, and per-route access controls. we'll include the SSO guide link.

[05:10] Ravi Kapoor: cost question - for Dedicated plus burst, how do you peg the extra capacity and what are pricing implications?
[05:22] Lena Park: two options: reserved Dedicated nodes for steady baseline and a burst pool for short spikes billed at higher unit rate. we'll provide a pricing sheet; Marcus also noted quantized variants reduce unit cost but have slight quality delta.
[05:38] Marcus Chen: tradeoff is you can run a quantized 4-bit variant in burst for cost saving, but we recommend canarying that separately because of subtle output differences.

[06:05] Emily Santos: runbook walkthrough next - can you go through the cutover checklist?
[06:12] Lena Park: sure. Step 0: freeze config changes. Step 1: staging smoke test - run full regression suite. Step 2: deploy new model variant to canary ring (5%), step 3: monitor metrics + probe prompts for 2 hours, step 4: if green, ramp to 25% then 50% using automated policy with 15min observation windows, step 5: full cutover and deprecate old route after 24 hours of stable metrics. rollback steps include immediate traffic diversion to previous model and alerting on-call.
[06:45] Marcus Chen: add: pre-cutover checklist should include KV cache warming scripts for top 500 prefixes, to avoid cold-cache spikes. that's the script I'll share.

[07:05] Jordan Lee: what's the recommended maintenance window? our peak is 12-6 UTC.
[07:12] Marcus Chen: recommend 02:00-04:00 UTC to minimize user impact. canary can run earlier as well, but full ramp ideally in low usage window.

[08:10] Emily Santos: for monitoring, what dashboards will we need and who on our team gets which alerts?
[08:18] Lena Park: dashboards: latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, token cost per minute, model quality probe score, throughput. alerts: critical (auto-rollback) to on-call, warn alerts to devs/SE. we can set PagerDuty integration.
[08:40] Priya Desai: audit logs need to include request IDs and user identifiers for traceability. also need encryption-at-rest and in transit confirmed.
[08:55] Lena Park: confirmed - TLS in transit and encryption-at-rest with customer-managed KMS for Private/Dedicated. we'll document specifics.

[10:00] Ravi Kapoor: one more thing on A/B testing - can we run A/B for a subset of flows while keeping others on the old model?
[10:12] Marcus Chen: yes routing policies can be per-route, so you can A/B specific endpoints. use consistent hashing if you want sticky sessions.
[10:25] Jordan Lee: we'd like to test quantized variant on low-risk flows first.
[10:30] Marcus Chen: makes sense, treat quantized as separate canary variant and monitor quality probe closely.

[12:05] Lena Park: timeline check - Beacon team to confirm maintenance window and sign-off by Friday 2026-06-27, Redwood to deliver runbook + scripts by Friday and pricing by Monday.
[12:20] Emily Santos: we'll aim for that; security needs to review the runbook and KMS details.

[13:00] Priya Desai: what about fallback models in case of capacity issues? can Redwood route to a smaller model or different region automatically?
[13:12] Marcus Chen: yes routing policy supports fallback tiers: same region lower-capacity variant, or cross-region fallback. fallback increases latency but preserves availability. we can configure cost thresholds to trigger fallback.

[15:00] Ravi Kapoor: small point, the probe prompts sometimes false positive on edge cases. can we configure the threshold and also allow manual ack to bypass immediate rollback?
[15:15] Marcus Chen: yes thresholds are adjustable; we can set a two-stage rollback where first stage sends an ops paging and requires manual ack before full traffic diversion. we'll include that in the runbook.

[18:00] Lena Park: action items recap: Lena send runbook, Marcus share KV warming script and canary automation, Emily confirm window, Priya share KMS/audit requirements. any other open items?
[18:20] Jordan Lee: one ask - can you provide an estimated token cost delta for 5%, 25% canary?
[18:30] Lena Park: yes we'll run cost projection and include in pricing doc.

[19:00] Ravi Kapoor: timeline for go-live after canary success? how fast can we ramp to 100%?
[19:10] Marcus Chen: operationally we recommend progressive ramp over 24 hours, but technically you can ramp faster. we'll follow your risk appetite.

[20:00] Lena Park: okay if no more questions, we'll wrap and follow the next steps.

Recap and next steps: Lena to share runbook and pricing, Marcus to send canary scripts and KV warm up, Beacon to confirm window and on-call. Schedule on-call runthrough before cutover.

End of transcript.
